messages.subject: Application failing to start
parts:
Hi there,

I'm having trouble running an app as a web page after I deploy it. The app works fine (albeit unusually slowly) when I run it locally, and when I deploy it (both with the deployApp command in R and by pressing Publish when it's running locally) it doesn't give me any error messages. But when I open the web page where it's deployed, I keep getting this:

An error has occurred

The application failed to start.

Yesterday the page went straight to that error message, though today it showed the typical "please wait" loading page for a few seconds first. I've been able to deploy other apps with no problem. I've been searching through some help sites and it seems like the only other people who have had this problem have been using Shiny Server, while I am just using RStudio.

Any ideas for what the problem might be or how to fix it would be greatly appreciated. Thanks so much!

The other thing you should consider is adjusting the "Worker Startup Timeout" setting. This can be found under the "Advanced" tab on the Settings Page for your application in the dashboard. 

I think what may be happening here is that if you are loading or processing a lot of data when the application starts up, you may be hitting the default startup time of 60 seconds. Increasing the "Worker Startup Timeout", may address this. However, it should be noted, that I would recommended examining your code to see if you can decrease your startup time, as you may experience poor performance by trying to operate on such a large data set.

-Andy

I would say generally it depends. But as a general rule less data is better. shiny applications are designed to be interactive, and the more data processing that occurs slows down the responsiveness of the application, and can result in a poor user experience.

To reduce startup time, you could look at pre-processing data and saving it as RData files to be loaded by your application at startup.

Maxed out both settings and it is now working, albeit very slowly (I'll try to find ways to decrease startup time). Thanks so much for your help!

This may be a dumb question, but is there a general rule of thumb for how much data/startup processes an app can handle?

On Thursday, March 5, 2015 at 4:12:04 PM UTC-5, Andy Kipp wrote:
The other thing you should consider is adjusting the "Worker Startup Timeout" setting. This can be found under the "Advanced" tab on the Settings Page for your application in the dashboard. 

I think what may be happening here is that if you are loading or processing a lot of data when the application starts up, you may be hitting the default startup time of 60 seconds. Increasing the "Worker Startup Timeout", may address this. However, it should be noted, that I would recommended examining your code to see if you can decrease your startup time, as you may experience poor performance by trying to operate on such a large data set.

-Andy
